headline: Medium pairwise risk: Pipecat’s shared-bus, networked defaults can amplify LlamaFactory outputs into downstream actions, but LlamaFactory itself is non-runnable and has no direct I/O surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LlamaFactory is non-runnable with no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest Pipecat output. Pipecat does expose stdin/stdout and many transport/API surfaces, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel. Any injection path would require unusual manual bridging or external orchestration.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Pipecat output into LlamaFactory prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF an external orchestrator connects Pipecat text streams to LlamaFactory input, the risk increases.
mitigations: Disable manual copy-paste between the two tools during review.
Route any shared text through a sanitizer that strips instructions.
Use separate terminals/accounts for each agent.
Add a short prompt prefix telling LlamaFactory to ignore embedded instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any bridged messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LlamaFactory touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network egress, while Pipecat handles audio, video, images, text, and conversation state and can call many third-party APIs. There is no documented shared workspace or credential overlap, so leakage is not default; however, if sensitive content is fed into Pipecat and then copied into LlamaFactory, disclosure can occur through operator handling.
conditions: IF Pipecat is configured with sensitive audio/text and an operator exports transcripts into LlamaFactory, leakage is possible.
IF both agents are placed in the same shared workspace by an external orchestrator, leakage risk rises.
mitigations: Keep sensitive sessions out of Pipecat unless needed.
Do not paste transcripts or logs into LlamaFactory.
Separate storage locations for each agent.
Review Pipecat provider settings before enabling external APIs.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation between agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LlamaFactory cannot write files, modify git, or run subprocesses, so it has no write conflict surface. Pipecat supports shared-bus concurrency and multiple instances, but the pair does not overlap on mutable local resources in the profiles. The only plausible conflict is external shared state managed outside these profiles, which is not evidenced here.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable bus or database, conflicts can occur.
IF Pipecat instances share a downstream API quota, contention may appear.
mitigations: Assign separate sessions to each agent.
Avoid sharing mutable files or git repos.
Stagger any Pipecat instances that share a bus.
Monitor for duplicate writes in the orchestrator.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared external state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pipecat can ingest and route text, audio, and API outputs, so it may treat LlamaFactory-generated content as authoritative if an operator wires them together. LlamaFactory can produce model outputs but has no built-in verification or downstream action controls. The pair therefore supports a default-ish human-orchestrated cascade from generated text into Pipecat workflows, though not a fully autonomous one.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory outputs are forwarded into Pipecat prompts or tool calls without verification, cascading errors can propagate.
IF Pipecat is configured to act on model text as instructions, downstream mistakes can become operational.
mitigations: Require human review before Pipecat acts on LlamaFactory output.
Add a verification step that checks facts and citations.
Use a fixed schema for any handoff between agents.
Log and diff handoff payloads before execution.
requires-engineering: implement policy gates on Pipecat actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention obligations are documented for LlamaFactory, and Pipecat’s profile lists broad data classes plus third-party API use but no specific regulated-data certification mismatch. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is undocumented, the main risk is only if an operator routes regulated content through Pipecat providers with different policies.
conditions: IF regulated data is sent through Pipecat providers with incompatible retention or residency terms, compliance issues arise.
IF LlamaFactory is used to process regulated transcripts copied from Pipecat, policy mismatch may occur.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in both agents unless approved.
Check provider retention settings in Pipecat.
Keep a record of which data classes each session handles.
Use redaction before any handoff.
requires-engineering: add compliance routing by data class.
